question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? The astronomers Annie and Edward Maunder carefully combed through old records documenting the dark patches called sunspots that appear on the sun's surface. In the late nineteenth century, their research pinpointed a stretch of years running from 1645 to 1715--today referred to as the Maunder ______ sunspots were remarkably rare, an occurrence that solar physicists are still working to explain.
option a: Minimum when
option d: Minimum: when
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma correctly attaches the supplementary 'when' clause to the naming phrase 'the Maunder Minimum.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The Mars Curiosity rover, launched in 2011, carried an onboard laboratory that let it examine rock samples right where it found them, yet it had no way to store those samples for later study. ______ as they developed the 2020 Mars Perseverance rover, robotics technologist Shreyansh Daftry, along with fellow members of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, aimed to build in a mechanism capable of doing precisely that.
option a: Specifically,
option d: Hence,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Hence' signals that designing a sample-storing mechanism was a consequence of Curiosity's inability to preserve samples.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? When Iestyn Barr and his fellow researchers mapped out the glacial history of Antarctica, they found that the Transantarctic Mountains--a range stretching 3,500 km across the continent--contain glaciers that are no less than 60 million years old. ______ the team concluded, glaciers existed in Antarctica well before the continent-spanning ice sheet took shape 34 million years ago.
option a: Thus,
option d: Even so,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Thus' shows the conclusion follows logically from the finding that some glaciers are at least 60 million years old.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Writing in a 1948 piece titled "The Language of Lines," the Brazilian photographer Jose Yalenti contended that what raises black-and-white photography to the level of fine art is its distinctive--and, as he saw it, superior--handling of lines. ______ Yalenti maintained that using linear forms to convey perspective is photography's "indisputable and exclusive domain," producing a visual language that outdoes even the work of celebrated painters.
option a: However,
option d: In any case,
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Indeed' reinforces and intensifies the preceding claim about lines elevating photography to fine art.

question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two sculptures. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: I Call Your Image to Mind..., a 2004 work by the Welsh artist Cerith Wyn Evans, is made of white neon lighting arranged to spell out its title phrase ("I call your image to mind"). Ginger, a 2023 work by the Japanese artist Rikako Kawauchi, is made of pink neon lighting shaped into an abstract squiggle.
option a: Both Evans's and Kawauchi's sculptures are crafted from neon lighting.
option b: Kawauchi's sculpture Ginger consists of pink neon lighting in an abstract squiggle shape.
option c: The neon lighting in I Call Your Image to Mind... is white, but the lighting in Ginger is pink.
option d: Rather than spelling out a phrase, Kawauchi's sculpture forms an abstract squiggle shape.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice A names the shared trait, that both sculptures are made of neon lighting.

question: The student wants to compare the length of time Laura J. Hecox and Catherine A. Moore worked as lighthouse keepers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: At night, lighthouses give off vital light signals that guide ships and other watercraft as they navigate. Before automation, each lighthouse was run by a lighthouse keeper. Laura J. Hecox served as the keeper of Santa Cruz Light in California, a post she held for thirty-four years (1883-1917). Catherine A. Moore served as the keeper of Black Rock Harbor Light in Connecticut, a post she held for sixty-one years (1817-1878).
option a: From 1883 to 1917, the nighttime waters of California were more navigable thanks to lighthouse keepers Laura J. Hecox and Catherine A. Moore.
option b: Laura J. Hecox and Catherine A. Moore were both lighthouse keepers at a time when such a person was needed to operate a lighthouse.
option c: Laura J. Hecox worked as a lighthouse keeper for thirty-four years, but Catherine A. Moore did so for even longer: sixty-one years.
option d: Before automation, lighthouse keepers like Laura J. Hecox, who served for thirty-four years, and Catherine A. Moore were crucial to ensuring safe navigation for watercraft.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice C directly compares the two keepers' tenures, thirty-four years versus sixty-one.

question: The student wants to indicate the location of the East Falkland Isthmus. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: An isthmus--also called a land bridge--is a narrow strip of land that links two larger landmasses across a stretch of water. The East Falkland Isthmus joins Lafonia to the northern portion of East Falkland. The East Falkland Isthmus lies within the Falkland Islands.
option a: The East Falkland Isthmus is located in the Falkland Islands, where it connects Lafonia to the northern part of East Falkland.
option b: One example of an isthmus is the East Falkland Isthmus.
option c: An isthmus, also known as a land bridge, is a strip of land that connects two larger pieces of land across an expanse of water.
option d: An isthmus, or land bridge, like the East Falkland Isthmus, connects two larger pieces of land.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only choice A states where the isthmus is located, in the Falkland Islands.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Microplastics are a frequent pollutant of vast bodies of water such as oceans. Because particles occur in high concentrations and show ______ among themselves--differing in size, shape, and material--thoroughly categorizing all the microplastics in a water sample is burdensome, so Ojeda-Benitez et al. are investigating a device to help quickly and accurately identify certain characteristics.
option a: incompatibilities
option d: restraints
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Inconsistencies' matches the described variations in size, shape, and material among the particles.

question: As used in the text, what does the word "mastery" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Alice Dunbar Nelson's 1899 short story "The Fisherman of Pass Christian." Pass Christian is a city in the US state of Mississippi. Along the shore at Pass Christian, the quick breezes collide and clash, each seeming to fight for the mastery of the air. Down through the pines drifts the land-breeze--cold, fragrant, and resinous--carrying almost living memories of shadowy woods darkened beneath countless pine-needles. From the south rises the Gulf breeze, warm, soft, and languorous, hinting at tropical heat.
option a: Familiarity
option d: Skillfulness
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The breezes struggle for control of the air, so 'mastery' means domination.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase? Dinosaur exhibits at institutions like the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County in Los Angeles--whose holdings include a mounted Allosaurus fragilis skeleton--stand out for the ______ of the research that underlies them: to ensure the exhibits' accuracy, the museum's staff drew on a great many sources.
option a: shallowness
option d: rigor
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Consulting numerous sources for accuracy signals the 'rigor,' or thoroughness, of the research.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole? Going beyond a straightforward "present or absent" label, researchers developed a new classification system that permits a more nuanced understanding of bioluminescence in marine organisms than binary systems ever allowed. The new six-point scale weighs the differing degrees of supporting evidence used to confirm that a species is bioluminescent. For instance, the splendid ponyfish earns a 1 because of inconsistent reports, the emperor squid earns a 4 because it anatomically resembles known luminous relatives, and the violet cod earns a 6 thanks to verified direct observations.
option a: It explains the basis for the new system's scoring criteria.
option b: It explains how the new classification system was derived from the previous binary system.
option c: It justifies the need for a new classification system for marine species.
option d: It emphasizes the thoroughness of the research conducted.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined sentence explains that scores reflect differing levels of supporting evidence, the basis of the scoring criteria.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Although adult glass eels can be found off the coast of Maine, the eels actually begin life in the Sargasso Sea--a biologically rich region of the North Atlantic Ocean where they are born and to which they later return to breed. Biologists think they have identified the broad zone within the Sargasso Sea that is vital to the endangered eels' survival, yet how the animals spawn there remains largely unknown. Researchers expect that solving this mystery will improve conservation of glass eels and their habitat, helping in turn to sustain several other species that depend on the eels as a food source.
option a: It presents a finding from a study that identifies the circumstances required to ensure the survival of glass eels.
option b: It indicates that the benefit of understanding glass eels' spawning behavior extends beyond the eels.
option c: It suggests that scientists are more concerned about other species than about glass eels' habitat.
option d: It discusses a role that glass eels and other species serve in supporting the ecosystem of the Sargasso Sea.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined portion shows the payoff reaches beyond the eels to other species that feed on them.

question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text? The following text is adapted from Henry James's 1916 short story "The Pupil." A man is being considered for a position as a live-in tutor for a woman's child. The poor young man kept faltering and putting it off: raising the matter of terms--speaking of money to someone who spoke only of feelings and, as it were, of the aristocracy--cost him such an effort. Yet he was reluctant to leave, treating his engagement as settled, without some more conventional reference to that subject than the manner of the large, affable lady gave him an opening for; she sat there drawing a pair of soiled suede gloves through a jewelled hand and, at once insistent and evasive, said over and over everything except the thing he would have liked to hear.
option a: It criticizes a person for being excessively timid.
option b: It draws a sharp contrast between the personalities of two people.
option c: It describes a person's unsuccessful attempt to change someone's mind.
option d: It portrays the difficulty a person has with raising a topic of conversation.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The passage centers on the young man's struggle to bring up the subject of money.

question: Which statement about the Museo de Las Americas is best supported by the text? Established in 1991, the Museo de Las Americas presents art from Latin America, including the art of Indigenous peoples. Located in Denver, it holds a collection of more than 4,800 objects. Since 2000, several other institutions dedicated to Latino cultures have opened across the United States. Casa de Rosado in Lansing, Michigan, is one notable instance; it centers on the arts and cultures of Michigan's Latino communities.
option a: It is visited by more people than any other Latino cultural institution in the US.
option d: It is no longer located in Denver.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text directly states the collection contains more than 4,800 objects.

question: What does the text most directly suggest about translation apps? The linguist John McWhorter maintains that translation apps for smartphones and computers--even though they typically miss many subtleties--are increasingly eliminating the need to learn new languages. Improvements in language-processing technology have sharply increased how useful these apps are for routine tasks, such as asking about a dish on a menu, and for brief exchanges; even so, deeper communication (as in business dealings or meaningful personal exchanges) frequently depends on conversational patterns and fine shades of meaning.
option a: They are coming to be embraced by international tourists but are viewed with skepticism by many business professionals.
option b: They have improved remarkably over time but remain insufficient to support the complexity called for in certain interactions.
option c: They are becoming simpler to use but are inconsistent in how comprehensively they cover different languages.
option d: They have gained impressive capabilities but continue to be widely viewed as inadequate for most practical purposes.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The apps have improved greatly yet fall short for richer, more complex communication.

question: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the statement? Mean Adhesion Strength of Graphite and Acrylamide Gel, at Varying Voltages (graph; x-axis Voltage (V), 0 to 3; y-axis Adhesion strength (kPa), 0 to 45; series: graphite-AAm pair). Wenhao Xu and coworkers showed that subjecting graphite (a conductor) and an acrylamide (AAm) gel to a low direct-current electrical field can strengthen how firmly materials stick together. At certain voltages, adhesion strength--gauged in kilopascals (kPa) of stress required to pull the materials apart--was substantial (above 30 kPa). Applying a direct-current field at a positive voltage is not by itself enough to boost adhesion, however, as shown by the fact that ______
option a: at 1 V, mean adhesion strength was approximately equal to adhesion strength at 0 V.
option b: at 3 V, mean adhesion strength reached its highest observed level at approximately 30 kPa.
option c: at 0 V, mean adhesion strength was equal to 0 kPa.
option d: at 2 V, mean adhesion strength was lower than it was at both 1 V and 3 V.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Adhesion at 1 V being about the same as at 0 V shows positive voltage alone does not raise adhesion.

question: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student's claim? Members of the Girl Scouts of America, by Age Category, 1992-1995 (in thousands). Category | 1992 | 1993 | 1994 | 1995. Cadettes (11-14 years) | 188 | 168 | 174 | 172. Juniors (8-11 years) | 870 | 791 | 756 | 727. Brownies (6-8 years) | 1,319 | 1,225 | 1,181 | 1,142. Daisies (5-6 years) | 207 | 191 | 190 | 195. The Girl Scouts of America is well known for its yearly sales of several kinds of cookies, Tagalongs among them. A student writing an essay on the organization's history claims that between 1992 and 1995 the organization's popularity consistently reached its high point among members in a particular age range before falling off among older members as Girl Scout activities began competing with other interests.
option a: Only once between 1992 and 1995 did the number of Juniors in the Girl Scouts exceed the number of Brownies.
option b: There were 1,319,000 Brownies in the Girl Scouts in 1992 but 1,142,000 in 1995.
option c: For each year from 1992 to 1995, there were fewer Juniors in the Girl Scouts than there were Brownies.
option d: Throughout the years from 1992 to 1995, the number of Daisies in the Girl Scouts exceeded the number of Juniors.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Fewer Juniors than Brownies every year supports the claim that membership peaked among younger Brownies and then declined among older members.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Mia Heavener's 2019 novel Under Nushagak Bluff, which unfolds in the mid-twentieth century in a rural Alaskan fishing ______ the story of three Yup'ik women who contend with the rise of commercial fisheries and other changes affecting their community.
option a: village. Tells
option d: village, tells
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A comma closes the nonrestrictive 'which' clause, letting 'tells' serve as the main verb without a comma splice or fragment.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Numerous works by the Greek dramatist Menander (4th century BCE) have been ______ his Dyskolos, a comedy about a misanthrope, survives as an extant work: it can still be read.
option a: lost and conversely,
option d: lost, and conversely
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A period separates the two independent clauses, and 'Conversely' correctly opens the contrasting sentence.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Sergeant First Class Modesto Cartagena served in the United States 65th Infantry Regiment, a Puerto Rico-based regiment of the US Army. In 2016, the United States Congress recognized Cartagena and the other servicepeople of the 65th Infantry Regiment with one of its highest ______ Congressional Gold Medal.
option a: honors; the
option d: honors (the
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon properly introduces the specific award that names one of Congress's highest honors.
